verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Using the Cable Routing Legend (p.4): the roof-plan diagram (p.9) shows AC cable (purple) leaving the new-panel array toward an 'Out' point; a photo on the same page shows the purple-annotated route down the building corner past the AC condenser units; p.10 continues the same purple line along a side path ending at a gray junction/panel box on the wall, captioned 'AC cable is already connected for the existing system'; separately, the panel diagram (p.11) shows an internal arrow from 'Main Meter' to 'Solar Meter' via the bus bar chamber; earthing routes (orange/green, p.12-p.15) similarly run continuously from an 'LA' marker on the roof plan down the building side to 'LA Pit'/'AC Earth Pit' markers on bare ground. Each colored line continues logically from one photo/diagram to the next per the legend, with no visible orphan ends or unexplained size changes in the exposed sections shown.
verdicts.rationale: The color-coded routing (per the legend on p.4) is traceable continuously across the roof-plan diagram and the sequence of annotated site photos, from the panel array down the building to the meter board / earth pits, with each segment picking up where the previous one ends. This is a microinverter (Enphase) system, so there is no separate central-inverter DC run to trace beyond the per-panel AJB already noted as existing; the one connection not shown by a dedicated photo (junction box on p.10/p.14 to the Main Meter board on p.11) is explicitly described in the report text as an existing, already-connected run, which is a reasonable basis for continuity in an upgrade project rather than a gap.
